Look good to me, 2 cents:
1. Should we introduce a wrapper `RunWithContextString`? It would save a lot of code like `new(strings.Builder)` and `stdout.Reset()`
2. Should we remove all `Timeout: -1`, and then treat the default zero value as the default timeout (defaultCommandExecutionTimeout)? And currently the zero value doesn't have clear meaning, when it is used by `context.WithTimeout`, zero means timeout immediately, which is meaningless.

If some one want to run a git command for long time, they could set their own Timeout (100 or 99999 years if they like), but not infinity. So I think we do not need another no-timeout option now.

Or Gitea can provide a const like MaxDuration = the-max-duration-value, then `Timeout: git.MaxDuration` is more clear.
